manifesto.title: Rest is not a luxury. It is a necessity.

01.title: Slowness is a choice
01.body: We promise the opposite of a crowded schedule: morning practice, long meals, and quiet hours spent between the sea and the olive groves.

02.title: Same team, same calm
02.body: Every camp is held at the same stone hotel, with the same small team — a familiarity that never changes from one camp to the next.

03.title: We set the structure
03.body: You set the rest — your breath, your pace, your quiet. You are not arriving at a class; you are arriving at a retreat.

items.1: Accommodation in a stone hotel, shared room
items.2: Two yoga or pilates sessions a day
items.3: Three home-style, seasonal meals a day
items.5: Walks to Assos and Kadırga Bay

deepenPractice.title: Deepen Your Practice
deepenPractice.body: Morning and evening sessions run in groups that never exceed sixteen people. Our teachers know every body starts from a different place; the program is open from complete beginners to advanced practitioners.

nourishBody.title: Nourish Your Body
nourishBody.body: Our kitchen follows the season: olive oil, homemade cheese, vegetables from the garden. All three meals are eaten at a shared table, unhurried.

resetMind.title: Reset Your Mind
resetMind.body: Phones are set aside. Breathwork, long silences and empty hours by the pool give the mind the rest it actually needs.

foodMoment.title: Olive oil, homemade cheese, a shared table
foodMoment.alt: A shared meal on the stone terrace

comingSoon.title: Assos is only the beginning
comingSoon.lede: With partner hotels and partner pilates teachers, future nature retreats will join the calendar.

venue.title: Karadut Taş Otel
venue.lede: A refuge in the stone architecture of Assos, surrounded by olive groves and Aegean light.
venue.body1: Karadut Taş Otel is a small stone building woven from the local stone of Büyükhusun village, surrounded by olive groves. Thick walls hold in summer's cool and winter's warmth; the same plain language of stone and wood carries through every corner.
venue.body2: Within walking distance of ancient Assos, and a short drive from Kadırga Bay. In the day's free hours you can head to the ancient city, the olive groves, or the bay's clear water.
venue.accommodationNote: For room types and accommodation details, please see the hotel's official site.

experience.title: A Day at Camp
experience.lede: From the quiet of the morning to the shared table at night — every camp has its own programme, but all of them are built at the same unhurried pace.
experience.dailyFlowNote: The flow below is a sample day from our featured retreat. Each camp's own programme is on its detail page.
experience.nutritionBody1: Meals are prepared in the hotel's own kitchen, following the season: olive oil, vegetables from the garden, homemade cheese. The menu leans vegetarian, and all three meals are eaten at a shared table, unhurried.
experience.nutritionBody2: If you're vegan, gluten-free, or have an allergy, just note it on the inquiry form and we'll arrange it with the kitchen in advance.

bringItems.5: A light jacket for cooler evenings
bringItems.6: Your own yoga mat (optional — one is provided at camp)

experience.levelsBody: Most retreats are open to every level, and our teachers adapt each pose to your body. If a specific retreat leans toward an advanced practice, we say so in its description — otherwise, never having done yoga or pilates before is not a barrier to joining.

about.title: EDEN Wellness Club
about.lede: Not a crowded agency — a retreat organiser working at the same stone hotel, with the same small team.
about.storyBody1: EDEN Wellness Club began with a small team of yoga and pilates teachers in Istanbul who wanted to take their own students out of the city. On our first visit to Karadut Taş Otel in Assos, we found the quiet and the stone architecture we were looking for — we've held our camps at the same hotel ever since.
about.storyBody2: We don't own the hotel — we're guests there, just like our participants. Our job is to build the programme, choose the teachers, and keep the group small; the hotel and Assos itself take care of the rest.

approachItems.1: Small groups: no more than sixteen people per camp, small enough that we know everyone's name.
approachItems.2: A steady team: the same teachers, the same hotel, a trust that carries from camp to camp.
approachItems.3: Leaving room for nothing: our goal is to make space for rest, not to fill the schedule.

about.whyAssosBody: Unlike crowded holiday resorts, Assos is still quiet. The ancient city, the olive groves and Kadırga Bay are all within walking distance of one another; the stone architecture holds in summer's cool and winter's warmth. That's why we hold our camps right here, and nowhere else.
about.whyAssosImageAlt: A bird's-eye view of Büyükhusun village and the olive groves
about.ctaBody: Whatever you're wondering about — choosing a camp, whether the level suits you, or getting to Assos — you can ask us directly.
